speaker: thomas_nashe
text: From Paul's to this door the grievance dressed itself. He began as a stationer's man, a warm bladder of tallow, and by Cornhill he smelled of ink and promised herrings.

speaker: will_kemp
text: A bladder of tallow is every chandler's boy south of the river. Give him gills. A salt-fish on a stall, weeping brine when a beadle coughs. That is a man a yard can hear.

speaker: thomas_nashe
text: A salt-fish. You have mended him. Give it me back. He weeps brine at a Latin noun, and the beard is still the one I brought.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Give it you back? The gills were mine. Will, bear witness. He had a bladder until I put a fish on the board.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: You put the gills on him. He has already worn them out of the room. Let him go.

speaker: thomas_nashe
text: He is not gone. He is pickled in his own gravity, and the improvement is mine. I stole it fairly, which is the only fair theft at this table.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Fair. You come in with empty pockets and go home in my fish. I contest the theft. I do not contest the supper.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Go on. I am here to keep the fish in the room, not to own it.

speaker: thomas_nashe
text: Then hear the clerk of the parish. A jest that crosses this board without a collar belongs to whoever salts it, and I have the salt.

speaker: will_kemp
text: The yard would have had the splash. You have had the adjective. I liked him better angry, and wet.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Say the fish again. I lost the brine when the clerk arrived.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Salt-fish. Stall-board. Brine when a beadle coughs. That is the whole of him, and it was mine.

speaker: thomas_nashe
text: And it is mine now, and it shall owe me rent. Your blank verse never had the patience to be so dull, and I thank you for the silence.

speaker: alice_brambleby
text: Elbows off the gravy. You may insult a man who is not here once the jug is safe.

speaker: thomas_nashe
text: The jug is a critic. Let it stay. He would have annotated the jug.

speaker: will_kemp
text: He is not at this supper. I am. Do not put the gravy on my gills.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leave the jug where she set it. I have scarcely a sentence in this, and I mean to keep it so.

speaker: alice_brambleby
text: I am bringing the paper, since none of you will end a sentence.

speaker: alice_brambleby
text: Two shillings and eightpence, and the jug. The paper is duller than either of you, and it has the advantage of being true.

speaker: thomas_nashe
text: Two shillings and eightpence. I have not got it, and I admire it. A sum that can end a sentence.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Admire it. I will not be the fish that pays for the stall.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leave the paper where she put it. It has won, and it did not raise its voice.

speaker: alice_brambleby
text: Master Shakespeare, you have said less than the jug. That is a good custom. Master Nashe, wit is not money. I have tried paying the brewer in it.

speaker: thomas_nashe
text: The brewer wants coin. The bill is the cleaner writing. Two and eight. I shall remember the figures and forget which of us ate.

speaker: will_kemp
text: You ate. I saw the gravy go. Do not put that on my fish.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The bill does not care who ate. I am not dividing it.

speaker: thomas_nashe
text: Then I shall love the bill and not pay it, which is my usual marriage.

speaker: alice_brambleby
text: You will not marry my bill at this board. Two shillings and eightpence, and the jug. I have set both down. I am not a court.

speaker: will_kemp
text: The paper can sit. I have no third image, and I will not fund the second.

speaker: thomas_nashe
text: I have the fish, the theft, and an empty purse, and the purse is the honest one of the three.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The purse, then. We are done improving a man who is not in the room.

speaker: alice_brambleby
text: Done is when the board is clear. I have ended the louder half. The paper can sit.
